purpose: Construction rationale and descriptive boundary notes moved out of the runtime catalogue on 2026-10-25. No code reads these fields; they document how each archetype's boundaries and layers were interpreted.

functional_details: External moisture protection and drainage required by project conditions; thin functional layers omitted from nominal resistance and quantities.
Ground contact, exposed plinth fraction and soil boundary supplied by the building model.

TABULA source topology has a completely conditioned basement (Tab.Building!AT814=C); the Swedish brochure identifies its ground-contact floor and external basement wall. Geometry still selects which reusable definitions are present.

The source Cellar code contradicts that topology. BETSI foundation U-values already include ground transfer (ISO 13370); no source cellar resistance or reduction factor is added to this nominal assembly.

The brochure prescribes internal placement; the workbook measure names stone-wool facade board at lambda 0.036. Existing generic stone-wool batts at lambda 0.036 and density 29 kg/m3 are an explicit internal-lining family adaptation, not an exact facade-board product match.
The added 13 mm gypsum is an EPSM finish assumption. Metal supports, fixings and junction thermal bridges are project details and are not quantified in this nominal planar recipe.

Internal insulation and gypsum require a wall that remains dry year-round and a project moisture assessment. No polyethylene vapour barrier or timber studs are assumed; wet or moisture-exposed basements require a different project solution.
Brick resistance is retained exactly as in the TABULA measure. No ventilated cavity is represented or thermally counted.
Brick ties, structural support and drainage/moisture interfaces require project-specific completion; this nominal representative is not a certified facade design.
Separator sheet, reinforcement, perimeter isolation, moisture control, available floor height and final finish are project completion inputs.

Baseline, ground-to-room: retained 160 mm concrete, 80 mm LECA fill, then 80 mm cement-finished concrete topping. The topping closes the previously exposed loose-fill surface.
Cement-finished concrete is a period-supported mineral finish; topping depth and the underlying LECA recipe remain representative EPSM assumptions.

LECA grade/compaction and the topping support, separation, reinforcement, movement joints and moisture conditions are project details. No steel or ancillary quantities are included in the topping concrete.

WINDOW.optical_convention: Whole-aperture equivalent with negligible opaque-frame solar gain; no duplicate geometric frame or bundled angular/shading reduction.
